title: Site Sherpa weekly pocket ops — Mar 15 2026
body:
Summary:
This is the Site Sherpa weekly pocket ops note for the Private Deploy team covering the week ending 2026-03-15. Focus this week: three live installs (Zenith, Arcadia, and Helix), two persistent customer blockers, and a pair of network edge cases that repeatedly surfaced during node scaling. Notes below consolidate standup highlights, customer escalations, mitigation attempts, and concrete action items for next week.

What happened this week (high level):
- Zenith (Tier 1 fintech, on-prem): Completed day-1 hardware validation. Hit recurring KV-cache mismatch on GPU restart cycles causing 10–30s tail latency spikes on large chat sessions. Observed subtle model warming behavior where warmup requests sometimes evicted recently cached prefixes. Collected trace logs and HV metrics.
- Arcadia (healthcare VPC): Deployment progressed to app-layer smoke tests but failed onboarding due to the customer's outbound HTTP proxy injecting TLS interception certs. Our control-plane client failed TLS fingerprint checks and refused to register. Customer security team is resistant to allow an exception.
- Helix (mid-market SaaS, air-gapped on-prem): Install stall caused by expired CA bundle on edge sidecar image; image verification failures blocked nodeagent start. The customer has strict air-gap policy; we coordinated an offline certificate rotation with their ops lead.
- Node scaling: Two customers reported packet loss spikes when autoscaler spins new nodes behind an in-house firewall appliance (vendor: FortiX variant). Packet MTU path discovery appears broken; we see fragmentation and TCP retransmit storms when sequence-length > 1500.

Standup / meeting notes (selected):
- Mon 03/09: Install prioritization walkthrough. Decided to reallocate one field engineer from Helix to Zenith for deep tracing on Friday. Action: Ben to prepare a replay harness. (JIRA-PD-7642)
- Wed 03/11: Arcadia security sync with customer SREs and their network vendor. Short-term workaround: pin control-plane to TLS v1.2 + custom CA bundle on customer side — security team evaluating.
- Thu 03/12: Runbook triage for restart behaviors. Discovered our restart hook that flushes KV cache runs before the model warmup completes; proposed ordering change.
- Fri 03/13: Post-mortem draft for last month’s MTU incident circulated; identified flaky PMTU tests in our qa perf-suite.

Customer blockers (actionable / escalated):
1) Arcadia proxy TLS interception (blocker): customer security will not add our CA to allow control-plane registration. Business impact: onboarding delay of >2 weeks if unresolved. Escalation path: Alice (account lead) and Lina to schedule exec-to-exec call; request alternative auth token exchange via signed JWTs over an allowed port. Temp mitigation: use pre-registered static node tokens inside their VPC (security sign-off pending). (JIRA-PD-7689)
2) Zenith KV-cache tail latency (medium blocker): causes brief service degradations under heavy chat workloads; not a full outage but customer SLA felt. We reproduced in staging with an instrumented kernel and saw cache eviction race during concurrent restart+batching. Root cause hypothesis: race between on-start cache warmup and runtime eviction thread.

Telemetry & debugging artifacts captured this week:
- kernel traces from Zenith (perf + eBPF sampling) saved to internal bucket (link in runbook).
- Helix offline cert bundle and install transcript appended to the customer handoff doc.
- PCAPs from two affected customers showing PMTU path blackholes attached to JIRA-PD-7642.

Workarounds attempted and results:
- For Zenith: temporarily increased warmup TTL and disabled aggressive eviction on the restart path — reduced spike frequency but not eliminated.
- For Arcadia: created a sidecar shim that tunnels registration over port 443 using SNI trick to bypass transparent proxy — security declined on principle (inspection still possible).
- For Helix: provided offline signed CA and short-lived token; customer ops performed manual import and nodeagent came up.

Open risks & loose ends:
- If PV/bonded-NIC configuration at a customer site is mis-specified, we can see intermittent NIC flaps during scaling that are hard to reproduce in lab. Need a small diagnostic agent to collect NIC counters pre/post scale event.
- Long-term: our restart ordering change could have unintended memory-pressure side effects on very small nodes (4/8GB). We should gate rollout behind a canary on Dedicated test pool.

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Ben Ortiz: Build a deterministic replay harness for the KV-cache warmup race and validate the proposed restart hook reorder. Due: 2026-03-22. Linked: JIRA-PD-7642.
- Lina Gomez: Lead exec escalation call with Arcadia security and legal to approve either CA exception or JWT token flow; prepare contingency note. Due: 2026-03-18.
- Milan Shah: Draft a lightweight diagnostic container that samples NIC counters and MTU on scale events; include a minimal upload to support bundle. Due: 2026-03-19.
- Evan Chu: Prepare canary rollout playbook for restart-order change and schedule baseline perf runs on Dedicated test pool. Due: 2026-03-21.
- Aisha Patel (me): Consolidate post-install runbook edits and publish a short checklist for field engineers (add explicit steps for CA import in air-gapped installs). Due: 2026-03-17.

Notes / decisions to surface to product & infra:
- Product: consider an optional control-plane registration mode for environments with TLS inspection (token exchange via pre-shared static node tokens) — request scoping and security review.
- Infra: add a PMTU/fragmentation check to the nightly qa perf-suite; current coverage is insufficient for the in-the-wild firewall variants we keep hitting.

Meeting cadence & next checkpoints:
- Daily standups continue; Site Sherpa weekly sync moves to Mon 09:30 PT.
- Exec escalation call for Arcadia scheduled tentatively for 2026-03-17.
- Technical deep-dive for KV-cache race on 2026-03-18 (Ben, Milan, and runtime owners).

Additional context / misc notes: 
- Customer empathy: Arcadia has strict compliance posture; keep workaround conversations framed as temporary while pursuing a secure, audit-friendly long-term solution.
- Documentation: small note on certificate expiry check was added to the air-gap install checklist after Helix; please review before next field run.

If you have follow-ups or missed items, drop them in the #private-deploy-site-sherpa Slack thread and tag the owner.

-- Aisha
